paper.task: Given an image x with spatial resolution H × W and C channels, predict the corresponding pixel-wise label map of size H × W (the final segmentation mask; the text mentions organ shape and boundaries).

components.name: input image x
components.what: input image x ∈ R^{H×W×C}

provenance.quote: Given an image x ∈ R H×W ×C with an spatial resolution of H × W and C num- ber of channels

components.name: Hybrid CNN-Transformer encoder
components.what: encoder: a CNN extracts a feature map from the input, 1×1 patches of that map are patch-embedded and encoded by L Transformer layers into z_L

provenance.quote: TransUNet employs a CNN-Transformer hybrid model where CNN is first used as a feature extractor to generate a fea- ture map for the input

components.name: CNN
components.what: feature extractor that generates a feature map for the input; its intermediate high-resolution feature maps are also used in the decoding path (architecture not stated)

provenance.quote: CNN is first used as a feature extractor to generate a fea- ture map for the input

components.name: Image Sequentialization
components.what: tokenization: the CNN feature map is split into a sequence of flattened 1×1 patches (in the pure-Transformer variant of Sec. 3.1 the raw image is split into P×P patches instead)

provenance.quote: Image Sequentialization. Following [4], we first perform tokenization … Patch embedding is applied to 1 × 1 patches extracted from the CNN feature map

components.name: Patch Embedding
components.what: trainable linear projection E of the vectorized patches into a D-dimensional space, plus learned position embeddings E_pos added (Eq. 1); output z_0

provenance.quote: We map the vectorized patches x p into a latent D-dimensional embedding space using a trainable linear projection

components.name: Transformer layer
components.what: ×L (the Transformer encoder); each layer = LN → MSA with residual, then LN → MLP with residual (Eq. 2–3); the last layer's output z_L is the encoded image representation

provenance.quote: The Transformer encoder consists of L layers of Multihead Self-Attention (MSA) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) blocks

components.name: Reshape
components.what: reshapes the hidden-feature sequence z_L ∈ R^{(HW/P²)×D} to H/P × W/P × D to recover spatial order

provenance.quote: After reshaping the sequence of hidden feature

components.name: Cascaded Upsampler
components.what: decoder: cascade of multiple upsampling blocks taking the feature from H/P × W/P to full resolution H × W, aggregating encoder features via skip-connections

provenance.quote: We introduce a cascaded upsampler (CUP), which con- sists of multiple upsampling steps to decode the hidden feature

components.name: upsampling block
components.what: repeated multiple times (count not stated); each block = 2× upsampling operator → 3×3 convolution layer → ReLU layer

provenance.quote: where each block consists of a 2× upsampling operator, a 3×3 convolution layer, and a ReLU layer successively

components.name: segmentation mask
components.what: final segmentation mask: pixel-wise label map of size H × W

provenance.quote: Our goal is to predict the corresponding pixel-wise labelmap with size H × W

components.name: position embeddings E_pos
components.what: learned position embeddings added to the patch embeddings (Eq. 1)

provenance.quote: we learn specific position embeddings which are added to the patch embeddings to retain positional information

components.name: addition of E_pos
components.what: element-wise addition of E_pos to the embedded patches, giving z_0

provenance.quote: z 0 = [x 1 p E; x 2 p E; · · · ; x N p E] + E pos ,

components.what: input of the l-th Transformer layer

contributions.text: Unlike existing approaches, self-attention (Transformers) is introduced into the encoder design

provenance.quote: Unlike existing approaches, our method introduces self-attention mechanisms into the encoder design via the us- age of Transformers

contributions.text: TransUNet: a hybrid CNN-Transformer encoder plus a cascaded upsampler, to compensate for the loss of low-level details and enable precise localization

provenance.quote: TransUNet employs a hybrid CNN-Transformer architecture as the encoder as well as a cascaded upsampler to enable precise localization

contributions.text: Cascaded upsampler (CUP): multiple upsampling steps that decode the hidden feature into the final segmentation mask, forming a u-shape with the hybrid encoder via skip-connections

provenance.quote: We introduce a cascaded upsampler (CUP), which con- sists of multiple upsampling steps to decode the hidden feature for outputting the final segmentation mask

the segmentation mask (pixel-wise label map) for that same example input
assets.note: must correspond to the example input image

unclear: The number of upsampling blocks in CUP is not stated (only 'multiple'); the number of Transformer layers L, the embedding size D, and the CNN architecture are not given either.

Which intermediate CNN feature maps (which resolutions) feed which upsampling blocks, and how they are merged with the decoder features (concatenation, addition, ...), is not stated; the text defers to Figure 1(b), which is not available in this blind run.
Whether CUP ends with a segmentation head (e.g. a 1×1 convolution to the number of classes, as in the naive baseline) is not stated; no such component is recorded.

It is unclear whether the reshape of z_L belongs to CUP or precedes it ('After reshaping ..., we instantiate CUP by cascading multiple upsampling blocks'); it is recorded as a top-level op between the encoder and CUP.

In the hybrid encoder patch embedding is applied to 1 × 1 patches of the CNN feature map, yet the text keeps the H/P × W/P notation for the encoded feature; the CNN's downsampling factor (the effective P) is not stated.

The naive-upsampling decoder baseline ('None': reshape, 1×1 convolution to the number of classes, bilinear upsampling to H × W) and the pure-Transformer encoder of Sec. 3.1 (patches taken from the raw image) are comparison variants, not parts of TransUNet; they are left out of the components and flows.

Novelty of the hybrid encoder: it is recorded as proposed because the text says 'our method introduces self-attention mechanisms into the encoder design' and lists it with CUP for 'the proposed TransUNet'; its parts (CNN, patch embedding following [4], Transformer layers) are recorded as reused.

Overview depth: the Transformer layer's inner parts (LN, MSA, MLP and the residuals of Eq. 2–3) and the upsampling block's inner layers (2× upsampling, 3×3 conv, ReLU) are collapsed into their parents and described in 'what'.
No loss function or training procedure is described in this text.
Text extraction artefacts: fractions are split across lines (HW / P 2, H / P, W / P), the layer index ℓ appears as a backtick, and a footnote marker '2' interrupts 're-shaping' in Sec. 3.1.

Added after critic round 1 (faithfulness correction): position embeddings (Eq. 1) and the Transformer layer's internal structure (Eq. 2-3) as explicit components; the text says this structure is illustrated in its Figure 1(a).
